notes:
Summary: mid-market product org building conversational helpdesk + search features. Started on Hosted API to validate prompts; now moving to Dedicated POC to hit 99th percentile latency and predictable unit costs.

POC scope (agreed):
- Dedicated pool: 2x GPU nodes (customer suggested A100-equivalent), single-tenant VPC egress rules.
- Canary plan: route 10% production-like traffic to Dedicated during test window, 90% to Hosted. Gradually ramp to 50% if KPIs hold.
- Fallback routing: automatic fallback to hosted-api model variant (routed by policy) on node failure or p95 latency > 300ms for >5m.
- Model variants: primary = rf-2-large-quant (on Dedicated), fallback = rf-1-medium (hosted). Also test lower-precision quantized variant to hit cost targets.
- Region failover: primary in us-west-2; failover to eu-west-1 for regional outage tests (data residency constraints noted — EU traffic must stay in EU if flagged).
- Rollback plan: immediate rollback = switch routing to hosted api + reduce batch sizes; follow-up mitigation = scale up Dedicated pool or route to cheaper model.

KPIs & constraints:
- Latency target: p95 < 220ms end-to-end for chat flows (50-token average).
- Throughput target: baseline 200 req/s steady-state; burst to 1k req/s for 10s.
- Cost sensitivity: aiming for < $0.003/token equivalent with batching + cache. If cost > expected, will push back on reserved commit.

Security notes / asks:
- Need SOC2 type II evidence, KMS integration for key wrapping, audit log format (token-level)? asked to map to internal SIEM.
- Data residency: EU customers routes must remain in EU; need clear routing policy controls.

Quotes from CTO on call: "We need predictable latency — not just averages. If Dedicated can't guarantee p95 at scale, we'll stick with hosted but with caching layers."

- Legal to review SOW + subscription terms.
- Confirm retention window & audit log export cadence.
